chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Abd Allah al-Basri, who said:
I asked him about a woman who died among men. He said: “She is wrapped and buried, and she is not given ghusl.”

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: What I act upon is what these reports contain, together with what we have previously presented in the narration of Abi al-Sabbah al-Kinani, Abi Bakr al-Hadrami, and Dawud ibn Sirhan: that when a man dies among women among whom he has no mahram, and a woman dies among men among whom she has no mahram and no husband, then she is to be buried as she is and not touched in any circumstance. And that is not contradicted by what he narrated:

key_terms.الْأَخْبَارُ: The transmitted reports or hadiths relied upon for the ruling.
key_terms.تُغَسَّلُ: She is given ghusl (ritual washing of the deceased).
key_terms.تُلَفُّ: She is wrapped or shrouded for burial.
key_terms.زَوْجٌ: A husband, who has legal standing in relation to the deceased wife.
key_terms.لَا تُمَسَّ: She is not to be touched.
key_terms.مَحْرَمٌ: A person with whom marriage is permanently forbidden, permitting certain forms of contact.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a woman dies among unrelated men and no mahram or husband is present to perform ghusl?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the legal ruling for handling the body of a deceased woman who dies among unrelated men. It states that in the absence of a mahram or husband, she is to be wrapped and buried without ghusl, reflecting the juristic concern for preserving bodily sanctity and the limits of lawful physical contact after death.
